title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from 1.1 and the neighbouring pages). Grothendieck is building an adequate equivalence relation on algebraic cycles that lies between linear (rational) equivalence and algebraic equivalence. A cycle on X is 'equivalent to 0' if it can be written z = Z(𝔙) where:
- T is a smooth projective parameter variety;
- Z is a cycle on X×T (equivalently Y×T), used as a correspondence from T to X;
- 𝔙 is a 0-cycle of degree 0 on T whose Albanese sum vanishes, S_T(𝔙) = 0 in Alb(T).
In modern terms, 𝔙 lies in the Albanese kernel T(T) = ker(alb_T : CH_0(T)_0 → Alb(T)). So N^i(X) = Σ_{T,Γ} Γ_*(T(T)), and the quotient A'^i(X) = CH^i(X)/N^i(X). The previous page showed N(X) is a subgroup, using T×T' and the cycles 𝔙×a', a×𝔙'.

This page.
(1) N(X) is graded; this is immediate.
(2) N(X) contains all cycles linearly equivalent to 0. Rational equivalence is exactly Z(𝔙) with T = P^1 and 𝔙 = (0)−(∞). Since Alb(P^1) = 0, every degree-0 0-cycle on P^1 has S = 0. A sentence beginning 'Thus N(X) is indeed a subgroup ...' is struck out.
(3) Start of the proof of contravariant functoriality: for f: X → Y, f^* maps N(Y) into N(X).
- Write z = Z(𝔙) with Z on Y×T and 𝔙 as in 1.1.
- Replace Z and 𝔙 by linearly equivalent Z', 𝔙'. Then Z'(𝔙') is linearly equivalent to z. Also 𝔙' still has degree 0 and S_T(𝔙') = 0, because the Albanese sum is invariant under rational equivalence.
- So it suffices to find Z', 𝔙' such that the pullback (f×id_T)^*(Z') = Z'_1 and the intersection Z'(𝔙') are both defined (a moving-lemma requirement).
- Intersection theory (compatibility of pullback with the correspondence action, using the margin diagram X×T → Y×T over T) then gives f^*(Z'(𝔙')) = Z'_1(𝔙').
- The left side represents f^*(z) in A^i(X). The right side is visibly of the form defining N(X).
The next page leaves the moving step 'à rédiger'. It then states Scholie 1.3: the A'^*(X) have the same functorial properties as Chow groups (including the projection formula), and coincide with the classical theory where linear and algebraic equivalence agree.

Modern comments on the resulting theory:
- On 0-cycles (take T = X, Γ = diagonal), A'_0(X) = Z ⊕ Alb(X)(k).
- On divisors, A'^1 = Pic, because any correspondence-induced map CH_0(T)_0 → Pic^0(X) factors through Alb(T).
- In general N lies in the kernel of every regular homomorphism, and conjecturally in the Bloch–Beilinson F^2.
errors: Notational slip: the text writes f^*(Z'(𝔙')) = Z_1(𝔙') where Z'_1(𝔙') is meant.

Gap acknowledged by the author: the existence of Z', 𝔙' making all intersections proper is not proved ('Nous laissons ici le détail'). With Chow's moving lemma on smooth projective varieties this is standard. In Fulton-style intersection theory it is unnecessary, since f^*∘Γ_* = (Γ_f^t∘Γ)_* by correspondence calculus.
The page tacitly uses the fact that rational equivalence of 0-cycles preserves the Albanese sum S_T. This is true but not stated.
Minor: proving N contains rational equivalence needs Z on X×P^1 with Z(0), Z(∞) defined. That matches the definition of rational equivalence, so it is fine.

ideas.what: Equivalence relation on cycles generated by images, under correspondences Γ ∈ CH(T×X), of the Albanese kernels of all smooth projective T. It is intermediate between rational and algebraic equivalence.
ideas.modern_name: Quotient of CH^i by Σ Γ_*(T(T)) (images of Albanese kernels); closely related to H. Saito's filtration and to the kernel of the universal regular homomorphism / algebraic representative (Murre)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Saito (Abelian varieties attached to cycles of intermediate dimension, ~1979); S. Saito (filtrations via correspondences, 1990s); Murre (algebraic representatives, 1983–85); Bloch (Albanese kernel T(X))
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in SGA/EGA to my knowledge

ideas.what: Rational equivalence is included in N because Alb(P^1) = 0.
Pullback compatibility f^*(Z(𝔙)) = (f×id)^*Z(𝔙) via moving cycles in their linear equivalence class.
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of correspondence action / adequate equivalence relation stable under pullback

missed.claim: An early (c. 1965–71) definition of an adequate equivalence 'A'^*' between rational and algebraic equivalence. It is defined by correspondences applied to degree-0 0-cycles with vanishing Albanese sum, together with the claim that it has full Chow-type functoriality. This anticipates H. Saito's and S. Saito's correspondence-defined filtrations and the 'CH modulo kernel of algebraic representative' viewpoint.
missed.quote: sur T=P^1, tout 0-cycle 𝔙 de degré 0 satisfait S_T(𝔙)=0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck considered the Albanese-kernel-generated equivalence (a first step of a Bloch–Beilinson/Saito-type filtration) as a cycle theory in its own right. This is historically relevant to the attribution of these filtrations. The page itself contains only routine verifications.

deep.surprise_reason: The verifications on this page are routine (subgroup, contains rational equivalence, pullback via moving lemma). The underlying definition, an equivalence via Albanese kernels and correspondences, is a mildly notable early appearance of an idea later developed by H. Saito, S. Saito and Murre. It is not a new result.
